algorithm.title: Evaluation of Presumed Urinary Tract Infection (UTI) in Children 2 Months to 2 Years Old Presenting With Unexplained Fever.

cell.label: Child 2 months to 2 years old with unexplained fever. Toxic appearance?
Assess UTI risk. Low risk?*
Consider close clinical follow-up.
Urinalysis (by bag) with microscopy, nitrite, and leukocyte esterase.
Urinalysis (by SPA or catheter) with microscopy, nitrite, and leukocyte esterase, and urine culture.
Urinalysis positive (pyuria and/or bacteriuria)?
No UTI. Consider other causes of fever. Close clinical follow-up.
Urine culture (by SPA or catheter) and antibiotics.
Hospitalize; urinalysis and urine culture (by SPA or catheter); IV antibiotics.
Urinalysis positive (pyuria and/or bacteriuria) and 50,000 cfu/mL or more of a uropathogen on urine culture?
Antibiotics for 7 to 14 days.
Renal and bladder ultrasound. Abnormal ultrasound or recurrent febrile UTI?
Close clinical follow-up; reevaluate within 48 hours of the next unexplained fever.
VCUG.

footnotes.footnote: *Low risk by the UTI risk assessment described in the text.
SPA, suprapubic aspiration; UTI, urinary tract infection; VCUG, voiding cystourethrogram.

algorithm.title: Approach to the Management of a Child With Suspected Urinary Tract Infection (UTI).

cell.label: Child with burning on urination, urgency, or frequency.
cell.path: Afebrile, no CVA tenderness, and no vomiting

cell.label: Urinalysis (by midstream clean catch, SPA, or catheter) with microscopy, nitrite, and leukocyte esterase, and urine culture.
Urinalysis (by bag) with microscopy, nitrite, and leukocyte esterase.
Urine culture and urinalysis by catheterized urine, SPA, or midstream clean catch. Admit for IV antibiotics until afebrile for more than 12 hours.
Urinalysis positive (pyuria and/or bacteriuria)?
No UTI. Consider other causes of the symptoms. Close clinical follow-up.
Urine culture (by midstream clean catch, SPA, or catheter) and antibiotics.
Urinalysis positive (pyuria and/or bacteriuria) and 50,000 cfu/mL or more of a uropathogen on urine culture?
Antibiotics for 7 to 14 days for febrile UTI; 4 days for cystitis.
Abnormal ultrasound or recurrent febrile UTI?
Close clinical follow-up; reevaluate within 48 hours of the next unexplained fever.
VCUG.

footnotes.footnote: CVA, costovertebral angle; SPA, suprapubic aspiration; UTI, urinary tract infection; VCUG, voiding cystourethrogram.
